name: remap_file_pages
synopsis: int remap_file_pages(void *addr, size_t size, int prot, size_t pgoff, int flags);
description: The remap_file_pages() system call rearranges pages of a file mapping to create a nonlinear memory layout, allowing nonsequential mapping of file pages. It requires an initial mapping with mmap(2) and is deprecated since Linux 3.16 due to limited use and inefficiencies.

parameters.name: addr
parameters.description: Address within a previously mapped region; specifies where to place the file pages.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Length of the region in bytes; must be a multiple of the system page size.

parameters.name: pgoff
parameters.description: File offset in units of the system page size.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags with the same meaning as for mmap(2), but only MAP_NONBLOCK is used.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: addr does not refer to a valid mapping created with the MAP_SHARED flag.
addr, size, prot, or pgoff is invalid.

bugs: This system call is deprecated since Linux 3.16 and emulated in kernel since 4.0, making it less efficient; it is only useful for certain in-memory filesystems and has limited applications, especially on 64-bit systems.
